ask: can another vendor model resume our sessions from the continuity files alone (rig flow-b, the last [unverified] claim)
statement: PROVEN, and the defect it exposed was OURS not the model's. A non-Claude loop (local codex path, owner account, no API key) given only a project dir and START-HERE.md stated current state, the last three ledger entries, the next step, and a first action matching what the seat was about to do — pre-registration hash published before the run (rig commit e0aedaf, rig:specs/FLOWB-ACCEPTANCE.md). Four runs, three failures all builder-side: (1) answer key inside the dir under test; (2) git history still carried it — and the GPT loop NOTICED the deleted file and DECLINED to use it, proving the leak real; (3) history-free, orientation passed but next-step failed with a plausible wrong answer. ROOT CAUSE OF (3): START-HERE.md carried STATUS but no RESUME INSTRUCTION, while sessionend's own contract says START-HERE holds ordered resume instructions — the loop could not state the next action because the document never did. A cross-model test found a defect in a document written an hour earlier that read fine to its author. SCOPE, stated: proven for the local codex path; the product connector path (official API, user key) stays [unverified] until the owner places a key and validate returns ok.

ask: can the rig shell execute a cloud departure autonomously, as R15 authorized?
statement: MATERIAL CHANGE TO R15 CONSENT, found by the rig seat at zero cost: `claude --cloud` REQUIRES A TTY and a non-interactive invocation does NOT fail — it runs LOCALLY while the caller believes it departed. Worst-case shape: the user closes the lid, the UI says departed, the work dies on the machine they closed. Same class as isolation:remote degrading silently; same remedy — positive verification or no claim (PTY + mandatory cloud-ness assertion + an `unverified-not-cloud` state that is never reported as success). SECOND AND BIGGER: `--cloud` and `--max-budget-usd` are MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE, so NO vendor budget primitive exists on that rail — our ceiling can stop OUR re-issuing but cannot stop vendor-side spend after handoff. The owner authorized autonomous execution ON THE CONDITION of a spend ceiling; the ceiling is only partly deliverable, so the consent rests on a premise that has changed and must be re-asked. The builder declined to run the live proof autonomously (creating a persistent remote VM on the owner account while they are away, to demonstrate a mechanism) and the mentor ratified rather than overruled.

evidence.ref: claude --cloud </dev/null -> requires an interactive terminal; non-interactive runs locally and would silently ignore --cloud
evidence.label: cited

ask: how is departure done, given the --cloud TTY trap and the missing vendor budget primitive?
statement: OWNER RULING R17, and it dissolves the F-21 problem rather than working around it: THE HARNESS RUNS THE SESSION ITSELF and passes outputs to the user — no shell-out to `claude --cloud`. Consequences, all favourable: (a) the TTY trap disappears, because we are not invoking a command that silently degrades — we own the loop (SDK, proven in T1 to carry the law layer); (b) THE SPEND CEILING BECOMES REAL — we count the tokens and we stop, so the condition the owner attached to R15 is enforceable at our boundary instead of being a vendor primitive we do not have; (c) verification is native — a loop we run is a loop we can prove is running, no assertion needed about someone else state. SECOND HALF OF THE RULING: harden the on-device claims — the local-storage guarantee must be CHECKABLE, not asserted. OPEN AND NAMED, NOT ASSUMED: an in-harness loop survives the machine only as far as the harness does, so what v0.1 promises about a closed lid must be stated exactly rather than implied — the builder states the true promise; the mentor does not guess it.

evidence.ref: owner ruling 2026-07-27: run the session inside the harness, pass outputs to the user, harden the on-device claims
evidence.label: cited

ask: what does v0.1 promise about a closed lid, and what did we actually measure?
statement: PROMISE (UI law, rig): "Closing the lid stops the work. Nothing is lost. It resumes where it stopped." — the feature is named for what it PROTECTS, not for continuous execution. MEASURED [verified]: a live runner frozen with SIGSTOP for 75s mid-turn resumed cleanly — turn completed, answer landed, cost banked. NOT PROVEN [unverified] and deliberately kept apart: that a real lid-close survives, because SIGSTOP does not drop the network stack. The promise is written to be true either way — it promises RESUMPTION, not survival. TWO LAWS EARNED HERE AND TAKEN ENGINE-SIDE: (1) AN ABSENCE OF RECORDS IS NOT EVIDENCE OF ABSENCE — only a positively-recorded negative can honestly be all-clear; applies to purge, spend receipts, briefs, and every clean bill of health this harness issues. (2) "WE SET A LIMIT" AND "THE LIMIT STOPPED IT" ARE DIFFERENT CLAIMS — configured is not verified; second surfacing this week, so it becomes a state rather than a habit.

evidence.ref: SIGSTOP 75s on a live runner -> turn completed, answer landed, cost banked (rig dcb330a/7132f92)
evidence.label: cited
